Both sweeps are 7-point Laplacian\n// stencils with clamped boundaries, so the fused operator has a radius of two.\n//\n// Each block owns a BX x BY column of the grid and marches along z, keeping a\n// sliding window of three z-planes of the concentration field and three\n// z-planes of the chemical potential in shared memory. cell\n__device__ __forceinline__ double chemPotential(const double cv, const double cxp, const double cxn,\n                                                const double cyp, const double cyn, const double czp,\n                                                const double czn, const Params p) {\n    const double cxx = (cxp + cxn - 2.0 * cv) * p.ix2;\n    const double cyy = (cyp + cyn - 2.0 * cv) * p.iy2;\n    const double czz = (czp + czn - 2.0 * cv) * p.iz2;\n\n    return 4.5 * ((cv + 1.0) * p.e_AA + (cv - 1.0) * p.e_BB - 2.0 * cv * p.e_AB)\n           + 3.0 * cv + cv * cv * cv\n           - p.gamma * (cxx + cyy + czz);\n}\n\n__global__ __launch_bounds__(BX * BY) void cahnHilliardStepKernel(const double* __restrict__ cold,\n   for (size_t y = 0; y < ny; ++y) {\n            for (size_t x = 0; x < nx; ++x) {\n                const size_t idx = idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny);\n                const double cv = c[idx];\n         printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option:                                                                \\\n            exit(1);                                                                                         \\\n        }                                                                                                    \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// 3D index calculation\ninline constexpr size_t idx3(const size_t x, const size_t y, const size_t z, const size_t nx, const size_t ny) noexcept {\n    return z * (nx * ny) + y * nx + x;\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// CUDA implementation\n//\n// The two sweeps of the original code (chemical potential, then concentration\n// update) are fused into a single kernel.  Both sweeps are 7-point Laplacian\n// stencils with clamped boundaries, so the fused operator has a radius of two.\n//\n// Each block owns a BX x BY column of the grid and marches along z, keeping a\n// sliding window of three z-planes of the concentration field and three\n// z-planes of the chemical potential in shared memory.  This way every mu\n// value is evaluated only once (apart from the one-cell x/y halo) while the\n// intermediate mu field never leaves the chip: global memory traffic per cell\n// update is one read of c plus one write of cnew.\n//\n// All floating point expressions keep the operand order of the scalar code.\n// The grid spacings enter only as the exact reciprocals 1/(dx*dx) etc.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#ifndef CH_BX\n#define CH_BX 32\n#endif\n#ifndef CH_BY\n#define CH_BY 8\n#endif\nstatic constexpr int BX = CH_BX;\nstatic constexpr int BY = CH_BY;\nstatic constexpr int CW = BX + 4;   // shared c tile width  (two-cell halo)\nstatic constexpr int CH = BY + 4;   // shared c tile height\nstatic constexpr int MW = BX + 2;   // shared mu tile width (one-cell halo)\nstatic constexpr int MH = BY + 2;   // shared mu tile height\n\nstruct Params {\n    int nx, ny, nz;\n    double ix2, iy2, iz2;   // 1/(dx*dx), 1/(dy*dy), 1/(dz*dz)\n    double gamma;\n    double e_AA, e_BB, e_AB;\n    double dtD;             // dt * D\n};\n\n__device__ __forceinline__ int clampi(const int v, const int lo, const int hi) {\n    return min(max(v, lo), hi);\n}\n\n// Chemical potential from the 7-point neighbourhood of one cell\n__device__ __forceinline__ double chemPotential(const double cv, const double cxp, const double cxn,\n                                                const double cyp, const double cyn, const double czp,\n                                                const double czn, const Params p) {\n    const double cxx = (cxp + cxn - 2.0 * cv) * p.ix2;\n    const double cyy = (cyp + cyn - 2.0 * cv) * p.iy2;\n    const double czz = (czp + czn - 2.0 * cv) * p.iz2;\n\n    return 4.5 * ((cv + 1.0) * p.e_AA + (cv - 1.0) * p.e_BB - 2.0 * cv * p.e_AB)\n           + 3.0 * cv + cv * cv * cv\n           - p.gamma * (cxx + cyy + czz);\n}\n\n__global__ __launch_bounds__(BX * BY) void cahnHilliardStepKernel(const double* __restrict__ cold,\n                                                                  double* __restrict__ cnew,\n                                                                  const Params p, const int zchunk) {\n    constexpr int CP = CW * CH;         // cells per shared c plane\n    constexpr int MP = MW * MH;         // cells per shared mu plane\n    __shared__ double sc[3 * CP];\n    __shared__ double smu[3 * MP];\n\n    const int nx = p.nx, ny = p.ny, nz = p.nz;\n    const int tx = static_cast<int>(threadIdx.x);\n    const int ty = static_cast<int>(threadIdx.y);\n    const int tid = ty * BX + tx;\n    constexpr int nthreads = BX * BY;\n    constexpr int LD_ITEMS = (CP + nthreads - 1) / nthreads;\n    constexpr int MU_ITEMS = (MP + nthreads - 1) / nthreads;\n\n    const int x0 = static_cast<int>(blockIdx.x) * BX;\n    const int y0 = static_cast<int>(blockIdx.y) * BY;\n    const int zs = static_cast<int>(blockIdx.z) * zchunk;\n    if (zs >= nz) return;\n    const int ze = min(zs + zchunk, nz);\n\n    const int gx = x0 + tx;\n    const int gy = y0 + ty;\n    const bool active = (gx < nx) && (gy < ny);\n    const size_t plane = static_cast<size_t>(nx) * static_cast<size_t>(ny);\n\n    // All in-plane addressing is independent of z, so it is resolved once here\n    // and kept in registers; the z-loop below only does loads, flops and stores.\n    int ldDst[LD_ITEMS];    // destination offset inside a shared c plane\n    int ldSrc[LD_ITEMS];    // source offset inside a global z-plane\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int k = 0; k < LD_ITEMS; ++k) {\n        const int i = tid + k * nthreads;\n        ldDst[k] = (i < CP) ? i : -1;\n        const int lx = (i < CP) ? (i % CW) : 0;\n        const int ly = (i < CP) ? (i / CW) : 0;\n        ldSrc[k] = clampi(y0 - 2 + ly, 0, ny - 1) * nx + clampi(x0 - 2 + lx, 0, nx - 1);\n    }\n\n    int muDst[MU_ITEMS];    // destination offset inside a shared mu plane\n    int muC[MU_ITEMS], muXp[MU_ITEMS], muXn[MU_ITEMS], muYp[MU_ITEMS], muYn[MU_ITEMS];\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int k = 0; k < MU_ITEMS; ++k) {\n        const int i = tid + k * nthreads;\n        muDst[k] = (i < MP) ? i : -1;\n        const int lx = (i < MP) ? (i % MW) : 0;\n        const int ly = (i < MP) ? (i / MW) : 0;\n        // Halo entries evaluate mu of the clamped in-domain cell, which is what\n        // the clamped boundary treatment of the second Laplacian requires.\n        const int qx = clampi(x0 - 1 + lx, 0, nx - 1);\n        const int qy = clampi(y0 - 1 + ly, 0, ny - 1);\n        const int cx = qx - x0 + 2;\n        const int cy = qy - y0 + 2;\n        muC[k] = cy * CW + cx;\n        muXp[k] = cy * CW + (clampi(qx + 1, 0, nx - 1) - x0 + 2);\n        muXn[k] = cy * CW + (clampi(qx - 1, 0, nx - 1) - x0 + 2);\n        muYp[k] = (clampi(qy + 1, 0, ny - 1) - y0 + 2) * CW + cx;\n        muYn[k] = (clampi(qy - 1, 0, ny - 1) - y0 + 2) * CW + cx;\n    }\n\n    // Load one clamped z-plane of c into the ring slot belonging to it.\n    // Slot invariant: sc slot s holds the most recently loaded plane q with q % 3 == s.\n    auto loadC = [&](const int zq) {\n        const int q = clampi(zq, 0, nz - 1);\n        const size_t base = static_cast<size_t>(q) * plane;\n        double* dst = sc + (q % 3) * CP;\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int k = 0; k < LD_ITEMS; ++k) {\n            if (ldDst[k] >= 0) dst[ldDst[k]] = cold[base + ldSrc[k]];\n        }\n    };\n\n    // Evaluate mu on plane q (plus a one-cell x/y halo) from the resident c planes.\n    auto computeMu = [&](const int q) {\n        const double* c0 = sc + (q % 3) * CP;\n        const double* cn = sc + (clampi(q - 1, 0, nz - 1) % 3) * CP;\n        const double* cp = sc + (clampi(q + 1, 0, nz - 1) % 3) * CP;\n        double* dst = smu + (q % 3) * MP;\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int k = 0; k < MU_ITEMS; ++k) {\n            if (muDst[k] >= 0) {\n                dst[muDst[k]] = chemPotential(c0[muC[k]], c0[muXp[k]], c0[muXn[k]], c0[muYp[k]],\n                                              c0[muYn[k]], cp[muC[k]], cn[muC[k]], p);\n            }\n        }\n    };\n\n    // Offsets of this thread's own cell in the shared tiles and in the output.\n    const int muCtr = (ty + 1) * MW + (tx + 1);\n    const int cCtr = (ty + 2) * CW + (tx + 2);\n    const size_t outOff = static_cast<size_t>(gy) * nx + gx;\n\n    // Prologue: make mu planes max(zs-1,0) and zs resident.\n    loadC(zs - 2);\n    loadC(zs - 1);\n    loadC(zs);\n    __syncthreads();\n    if (zs > 0) {\n        computeMu(zs - 1);\n        __syncthreads();\n        loadC(zs + 1);          // reuses the slot of plane zs-2\n        __syncthreads();\n    } else {\n        loadC(zs + 1);\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n    computeMu(zs);\n\n    for (int z = zs; z < ze; ++z) {\n        __syncthreads();\n        loadC(z + 2);           // reuses the slot of plane z-1\n        __syncthreads();\n        if (z + 1 < nz) computeMu(z + 1);\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        if (active) {\n            const double* m0p = smu + (z % 3) * MP;\n            const double* mnp = smu + (clampi(z - 1, 0, nz - 1) % 3) * MP;\n            const double* mpp = smu + (clampi(z + 1, 0, nz - 1) % 3) * MP;\n\n            const double m0 = m0p[muCtr];\n            const double mxx = (m0p[muCtr + 1] + m0p[muCtr - 1] - 2.0 * m0) * p.ix2;\n            const double myy = (m0p[muCtr + MW] + m0p[muCtr - MW] - 2.0 * m0) * p.iy2;\n            const double mzz = (mpp[muCtr] + mnp[muCtr] - 2.0 * m0) * p.iz2;\n\n            cnew[static_cast<size_t>(z) * plane + outOff] =\n                sc[(z % 3) * CP + cCtr] + p.dtD * (mxx + myy + mzz);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Initialize concentration field\nvoid initializeConcentration(std::vector<double>& c, const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz) {\n    const size_t vol = nx * ny * nz;\n\n    for (size_t z = 0; z < nz; ++z) {\n        for (size_t y = 0; y < ny; ++y) {\n            for (size_t x = 0; x < nx; ++x) {\n                const size_t idx = idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny);\n                // Generate pseudo-random value in [-1, 1]\n                const size_t linear_id = z * (nx * ny) + y * nx + x;\n                const double pseudo = ((((linear_id + 1) * 1299709) % vol) / static_cast<double>(vol));\n                c[idx] = -1.0 + 2.0 * pseudo;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<double>& c, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t nx, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t ny, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t nz) {\n    // Check for NaN or Inf\n    for (const auto& val : c) {\n        if (std::isnan(val) || std::isinf(val)) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed: found NaN or Inf value\\n\");\n            return false;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Check if values are in reasonable range for concentration field\n    // After Cahn-Hilliard evolution, values should typically remain bounded\n    double minVal = c[0];\n    double maxVal = c[0];\n    for (const auto& val : c) {\n        minVal = std::min(minVal, val);\n        maxVal = std::max(maxVal, val);\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Concentration range: [%.6f, %.6f]\\n\", minVal, maxVal);\n\n    // Values should generally stay within reasonable bounds\n    if (maxVal > 10.0 || minVal < -10.0) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: values out of expected range\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -x <num>     Grid size in X dimension (default: 64)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -y <num>     Grid size in Y argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t nx = 64;\n    size_t ny = 0;\n    size_t nz = 0;\n    int iterations = 20;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line                                                                     \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                                           \\\n            printf(\"CUDA error %s at %s:%d: %s\\n\", cudaGetErrorName(err_), __FILE__, __LINE__,               \\\n                   cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                                                \\\n            exit(1);                                                                                         \\\n        }                                                                                                    \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// 3D index calculation\ninline constexpr size_t idx3(const size_t x, const size_t y, const size_t z, const size_t nx, const size_t ny) noexcept {\n    return z * (nx * ny) + y * nx + x;\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// CUDA implementation\n//\n// The two sweeps of the original code (chemical potential, then concentration\n// update) are fused into a single kernel.  Both sweeps are 7-point Laplacian\n// stencils with clamped boundaries, so the fused operator has a radius of two.\n//\n// Each block owns a BX x BY column of the grid and marches along z, keeping a\n// sliding window of three z-planes of the concentration field and three\n// z-planes of the chemical potential in shared memory.                                                                \\\n            exit(1);                                                                                         \\\n        }                                                                                                    \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// 3D index calculation\ninline constexpr size_t idx3(const size_t x, const size_t y, const size_t z, const size_t nx, const size_t ny) noexcept {\n    return z * (nx * ny) + y * nx + x;\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// CUDA implementation\n//\n// The two sweeps of the original code (chemical potential, then concentration\n// update) are fused into a single kernel.  Both sweeps are 7-point Laplacian\n// stencils with clamped boundaries, so the fused operator has a radius of two.\n//\n// Each block owns a BX x BY column of the grid and marches along z, keeping a\n// sliding window of three z-planes of the concentration field and three\n// z-planes of the chemical potential in shared memory.  This way every mu\n// value is evaluated only once (apart from the one-cell x/y halo) while the\n// intermediate mu field never leaves the chip: global memory traffic per cell\n// update is one read of c plus one write of cnew.\n//\n// All floating point expressions keep the operand order of the scalar code.\n// The grid spacings enter only as the exact reciprocals 1/(dx*dx) etc.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#ifndef CH_BX\n#define CH_BX 32\n#endif\n#ifndef CH_BY\n#define CH_BY 16\n#endif\nstatic constexpr int BX = CH_BX;\nstatic constexpr int BY = CH_BY;\nstatic constexpr int CW = BX + 4;   // shared c tile width  (two-cell halo)\nstatic constexpr int CH = BY + 4;   // shared c tile height\nstatic constexpr int MW = BX + 2;   // shared mu tile width (one-cell halo)\nstatic constexpr int MH = BY + 2;   // shared mu tile height\n\nstruct Params {\n    int nx, ny, nz;\n    double ix2, iy2, iz2;   // 1/(dx*dx), 1/(dy*dy), 1/(dz*dz)\n    double gamma;\n    double e_AA, e_BB, e_AB;\n    double dtD;             // dt * D\n};\n\n__device__ __forceinline__ int clampi(const int v, const int lo, const int hi) {\n    return min(max(v, lo), hi);\n}\n\n// Chemical potential from the 7-point neighbourhood of one cell\n__device__ __forceinline__ double chemPotential(const double cv, const double cxp, const double cxn,\n                                                const double cyp, const double cyn, const double czp,\n                                                const double czn, const Params p) {\n    const double cxx = (cxp + cxn - 2.0 * cv) * p.ix2;\n    const double cyy = (cyp + cyn - 2.0 * cv) * p.iy2;\n    const double czz = (czp + czn - 2.0 * cv) * p.iz2;\n\n    return 4.5 * ((cv + 1.0) * p.e_AA + (cv - 1.0) * p.e_BB - 2.0 * cv * p.e_AB)\n           + 3.0 * cv + cv * cv * cv\n           - p.gamma * (cxx + cyy + czz);\n}\n\n__global__ __launch_bounds__(BX * BY) void cahnHilliardStepKernel(const double* __restrict__ cold,\n                                                                  double* __restrict__ cnew,\n                                                                  const Params p, const int zchunk) {\n    constexpr int CP = CW * CH;         // cells per shared c plane\n    constexpr int MP = MW * MH;         // cells per shared mu plane\n    __shared__ double sc[3 * CP];\n    __shared__ double smu[3 * MP];\n\n    const int nx = p.nx, ny = p.ny, nz = p.nz;\n    const int tx = static_cast<int>(threadIdx.x);\n    const int ty = static_cast<int>(threadIdx.y);\n    const int tid = ty * BX + tx;\n    constexpr int nthreads = BX * BY;\n    constexpr int LD_ITEMS = (CP + nthreads - 1) / nthreads;\n    constexpr int MU_ITEMS = (MP + nthreads - 1) / nthreads;\n\n    const int x0 = static_cast<int>(blockIdx.x) * BX;\n    const int y0 = static_cast<int>(blockIdx.y) * BY;\n    const int zs = static_cast<int>(blockIdx.z) * zchunk;\n    if (zs >= nz) return;\n    const int ze = min(zs + zchunk, nz);\n\n    const int gx = x0 + tx;\n    const int gy = y0 + ty;\n    const bool active = (gx < nx) && (gy < ny);\n    const size_t plane = static_cast<size_t>(nx) * static_cast<size_t>(ny);\n\n    // All in-plane addressing is independent of z, so it is resolved once here\n    // and kept in registers; the z-loop below only does loads, flops and stores.\n    int ldDst[LD_ITEMS];    // destination offset inside a shared c plane\n    int ldSrc[LD_ITEMS];    // source offset inside a global z-plane\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int k = 0; k < LD_ITEMS; ++k) {\n        const int i = tid + k * nthreads;\n        ldDst[k] = (i < CP) ? i : -1;\n        const int lx = (i < CP) ? (i % CW) : 0;\n        const int ly = (i < CP) ? (i / CW) : 0;\n        ldSrc[k] = clampi(y0 - 2 + ly, 0, ny - 1) * nx + clampi(x0 - 2 + lx, 0, nx - 1);\n    }\n\n    int muDst[MU_ITEMS];    // destination offset inside a shared mu plane\n    int muC[MU_ITEMS];      // offset of the evaluation point inside a shared c plane\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int k = 0; k < MU_ITEMS; ++k) {\n        const int i = tid + k * nthreads;\n        muDst[k] = (i < MP) ? i : -1;\n        const int lx = (i < MP) ? (i % MW) : 0;\n        const int ly = (i < MP) ? (i / MW) : 0;\n        // Halo entries evaluate mu of the clamped in-domain cell, which is what\n        // the clamped boundary treatment of the second Laplacian requires.\n        const int qx = clampi(x0 - 1 + lx, 0, nx - 1);\n        const int qy = clampi(y0 - 1 + ly, 0, ny - 1);\n        // Because the c tile is filled with clamped global coordinates, the\n        // neighbours of an evaluation point are simply the adjacent tile cells:\n        // tile cell (qx-x0+2)-1 holds c[clamp(qx-1)], and likewise for +1/y.\n        muC[k] = (qy - y0 + 2) * CW + (qx - x0 + 2);\n    }\n\n    // Load one clamped z-plane of c into the ring slot belonging to it.\n    // Slot invariant: sc slot s holds the most recently loaded plane q with q % 3 == s.\n    auto loadC = [&](const int zq) {\n        const int q = clampi(zq, 0, nz - 1);\n        const size_t base = static_cast<size_t>(q) * plane;\n        double* dst = sc + (q % 3) * CP;\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int k = 0; k < LD_ITEMS; ++k) {\n            if (ldDst[k] >= 0) dst[ldDst[k]] = cold[base + ldSrc[k]];\n        }\n    };\n\n    // Evaluate mu on plane q (plus a one-cell x/y halo) from the resident c planes.\n    auto computeMu = [&](const int q) {\n        const double* c0 = sc + (q % 3) * CP;\n        const double* cn = sc + (clampi(q - 1, 0, nz - 1) % 3) * CP;\n        const double* cp = sc + (clampi(q + 1, 0, nz - 1) % 3) * CP;\n        double* dst = smu + (q % 3) * MP;\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int k = 0; k < MU_ITEMS; ++k) {\n            if (muDst[k] >= 0) {\n                const int o = muC[k];\n                dst[muDst[k]] = chemPotential(c0[o], c0[o + 1], c0[o - 1], c0[o + CW], c0[o - CW],\n                                              cp[o], cn[o], p);\n            }\n        }\n    };\n\n    // Offsets of this thread's own cell in the shared tiles and in the output.\n    const int muCtr = (ty + 1) * MW + (tx + 1);\n    const int cCtr = (ty + 2) * CW + (tx + 2);\n    const size_t outOff = static_cast<size_t>(gy) * nx + gx;\n\n    // Prologue: make mu planes max(zs-1,0) and zs resident.\n    loadC(zs - 2);\n    loadC(zs - 1);\n    loadC(zs);\n    __syncthreads();\n    if (zs > 0) {\n        computeMu(zs - 1);\n        __syncthreads();\n        loadC(zs + 1);          // reuses the slot of plane zs-2\n        __syncthreads();\n    } else {\n        loadC(zs + 1);\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n    computeMu(zs);\n\n    for (int z = zs; z < ze; ++z) {\n        __syncthreads();\n        loadC(z + 2);           // reuses the slot of plane z-1\n        __syncthreads();\n        if (z + 1 < nz) computeMu(z + 1);\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        if (active) {\n            const double* m0p = smu + (z % 3) * MP;\n            const double* mnp = smu + (clampi(z - 1, 0, nz - 1) % 3) * MP;\n            const double* mpp = smu + (clampi(z + 1, 0, nz - 1) % 3) * MP;\n\n            const double m0 = m0p[muCtr];\n            const double mxx = (m0p[muCtr + 1] + m0p[muCtr - 1] - 2.0 * m0) * p.ix2;\n            const double myy = (m0p[muCtr + MW] + m0p[muCtr - MW] - 2.0 * m0) * p.iy2;\n            const double mzz = (mpp[muCtr] + mnp[muCtr] - 2.0 * m0) * p.iz2;\n\n            cnew[static_cast<size_t>(z) * plane + outOff] =\n                sc[(z % 3) * CP + cCtr] + p.dtD * (mxx + myy + mzz);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Initialize concentration field\nvoid initializeConcentration(std::vector<double>& c, const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz) {\n    const size_t vol = nx * ny * nz;\n\n    for (size_t z = 0; z < nz; ++z) {\n        for (size_t y = 0; y < ny; ++y) {\n            for (size_t x = 0; x < nx; ++x) {\n                const size_t idx = idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny);\n                // Generate pseudo-random value in [-1, 1]\n                const size_t linear_id = z * (nx * ny) + y * nx + x;\n                const double pseudo = ((((linear_id + 1) * 1299709) % vol) / static_cast<double>(vol));\n                c[idx] = -1.0 + 2.0 * pseudo;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<double>& c, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t nx, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t ny, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t nz) {\n    // Check for NaN or Inf\n    for (const auto& val : c) {\n        if (std::isnan(val) || std::isinf(val)) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed: found NaN         // cells per shared c plane\n    constexpr int MP = MW * MH;         // cells per shared mu plane\n    __shared__ double sc[3 * CP];\n    __shared__ double smu[3 * MP];\n\n    const int nx = p.nx, ny = p.ny, nz = p.nz;\n    const int tx = static_cast<int>(threadIdx.x);\n    const int ty = static_cast<int>(threadIdx.y);\n    const int tid = ty * BX + tx;\n    constexpr int nthreads = BX * BY;\n    constexpr int LD_ITEMS = (CP + nthreads - 1) / nthreads;\n    constexpr int MU_ITEMS = (MP + nthreads - 1) / nthreads;\n\n    const int x0 = static_cast<int>(blockIdx.x) * BX;\n    const int y0 = static_cast<int>(blockIdx.y) * BY;\n    const int zs = static_cast<int>(blockIdx.z) * zchunk;\n    if (zs >= nz) return;\n    const int ze = min(zs + zchunk, nz);\n\n    const int gx = x0 + tx;\n    const int gy = y0 + ty;\n    const bool active = (gx < nx) && (gy < ny);\n    const size_t plane = static_cast<size_t>(nx) * static_cast<size_t>(ny);\n\n    // All in-plane addressing is independent of z, so it is resolved once here\n    // and kept in registers; the z-loop below only does loads, flops and stores.\n    int ldDst[LD_ITEMS];    // destination offset inside a shared c plane\n    int ldSrc[LD_ITEMS];    // source offset inside a global z-plane\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int k = 0; k < LD_ITEMS; ++k) {\n        const int i = tid + k * nthreads;\n        ldDst[k] = (i < CP) ? i : -1;\n        const int lx = (i < CP) ? (i % CW) : 0;\n        const int ly = (i < CP) ? (i / CW) : 0;\n        ldSrc[k] = clampi(y0 - 2 + ly, 0, ny - 1) * nx + clampi(x0 - 2 + lx, 0, nx - 1);\n    }\n\n    int muDst[MU_ITEMS];    // destination offset inside a shared mu plane\n    int muC[MU_ITEMS];      // offset of the evaluation point inside a shared c plane\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int k = 0; k < MU_ITEMS; ++k) {\n        const int i = tid + k * nthreads;\n        muDst[k] = (i < MP) ? i : -1;\n        const int lx = (i < MP) ? (i % MW) : 0;\n        const int ly = (i < MP) ? (i / MW) : 0;\n        // Halo entries evaluate mu of the clamped in-domain cell, which is what\n        // the clamped boundary treatment of the second Laplacian requires.\n        const int qx = clampi(x0 - 1 + lx, 0, nx - 1);\n        const int qy = clampi(y0 - 1 + ly, 0, ny - 1);\n        // Because the c tile is filled with clamped global coordinates, the\n        // neighbours of an evaluation point are simply the adjacent tile cells:\n        // tile cell (qx-x0+2)-1 holds c[clamp(qx-1)], and likewise for +1/y.\n        muC[k] = (qy - y0 + 2) * CW + (qx - x0 + 2);\n    }\n\n    // Load one clamped z-plane of c into the ring slot belonging to it.\n    // Slot invariant: sc slot s holds the most recently loaded plane q with q % 3 == s.\n    auto loadC = [&](const int zq) {\n        const int q = clampi(zq, 0, nz - 1);\n        const size_t base = static_cast<size_t>(q) * plane;\n        double* dst = sc + (q % 3) * CP;\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int k = 0; k < LD_ITEMS; ++k) {\n            if (ldDst[k] >= 0) dst[ldDst[k]] = cold[base + ldSrc[k]];\n        }\n    };\n\n    // Evaluate mu on plane q (plus a one-cell x/y halo) from the resident c planes.\n    auto computeMu = [&](const int q) {\n        const double* c0 = sc + (q % 3) * CP;\n        const double* cn = sc + (clampi(q - 1, 0, nz - 1) % 3) * CP;\n        const double* cp = sc + (clampi(q + 1, 0, nz - 1) % 3) * CP;\n        double* dst = smu + (q % 3) * MP;\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int k = 0; k < MU_ITEMS; ++k) {\n            if (muDst[k] >= 0) {\n                const int o = muC[k];\n                dst[muDst[k]] = chemPotential(c0[o], c0[o + 1], c0[o - 1], c0[o + CW], c0[o - CW],\n                                              cp[o], cn[o], p);\n            }\n        }\n    };\n\n    // Offsets of this thread's own cell in the shared tiles and in the output.\n    const int muCtr = (ty + 1) * MW + (tx + 1);\n    const int cCtr = (ty + 2) * CW + (tx + 2);\n    const size_t outOff = static_cast<size_t>(gy) * nx + gx;\n\n    // Prologue: make mu planes max(zs-1,0) and zs resident.\n    loadC(zs - 2);\n    loadC(zs - 1);\n    loadC(zs);\n    __syncthreads();\n    if (zs > 0) {\n        computeMu(zs - 1);\n        __syncthreads();\n        loadC(zs + 1);          // reuses the slot of plane zs-2\n        __syncthreads();\n    } else {\n        loadC(zs + 1);\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n    computeMu(zs);\n\n    for (int z = zs; z < ze; ++z) {\n        __syncthreads();\n        loadC(z + 2); The Cahn-Hilliard benchmark now runs entirely on the GPU via CUDA.\n\n## What changed\n\n**`cahn-hilliard/cahn_hilliard.cpp`** — the two host sweeps (`computeChemicalPotential`, `cahnHilliardUpdate`) are replaced by a single fused CUDA kernel:\n\n- **Kernel fusion.** Both sweeps are 7-point Laplacians, so the composite operator has radius 2. Fusing them means the intermediate `mu` field never touches global memory: traffic per cell update is one read of `c` plus one write of `cnew` instead of five array accesses.\n- **Sliding z-window in shared memory.** Each 32×16 block owns an x/y tile and marches along z, holding a 3-plane ring of `c` (36×20) and a 3-plane ring of `mu` (34×18). Every `mu` value is evaluated once — the only redundancy is the one-cell x/y halo, i.e. 1.20 `mu` evaluations per cell update.\n- **Clamped boundaries.** The `c` tile is filled using clamped global coordinates, which makes tile neighbours automatically equal `c[clamp(x±1)]`; `mu` halo slots store `mu` of the clamped in-domain cell, which is exactly what the second Laplacian's clamped stencil needs. The z ring indexes clamped planes, so `mu[-1] == mu[0]` falls out naturally.\n- **Address hoisting.** All in-plane index/clamp arithmetic is resolved once into registers before the z-loop. This dropped register use from 62 to 40, which is what lets 3 blocks (1536 threads) run per SM — worth ~15%.\n- **z-slab decomposition.** z is split into slabs so small grids still produce enough blocks to fill the device, with slabs kept long enough (`nz/8` cap) that the sliding-window prologue stays a few percent of the work.\n- A warm-up launch precedes the timed region — CUDA 12's lazy module loading otherwise charged ~140 ms of one-time code loading to the first kernel.\n\n**`cahn-hilliard/CMakeLists.txt`** — enables the `CUDA` language, compiles the existing `.cpp` as CUDA via `set_source_files_properties`, and targets `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES native`. Executable name unchanged, no new files, no new dependencies.\n\n## Correctness\n\nEvery floating-point expression keeps the original operand order (`dx` etc. enter as exact reciprocals — the same value, since spacings are 1.0). To prove that rather than assert it, I built both versions with FMA contraction disabled (`-ffp-contract=off` / `--fmad=false`) and compared full result blocks including the FNV hash: **bit-identical** across 12 configurations, including odd/prime extents, degenerate 1×1×1, `nz=2`, thin slabs (`5×5×200`, `3×200×2`), and `-i 0`.\n\nIn the optimized builds the results differ from the CPU reference by 1–2 ULP (~1e-16 relative), because GCC and nvcc each contract FMAs independently — unavoidable, and the residual is the same magnitude as `-march=native` vs. plain `-O2` on the CPU alone. `compute-sanitizer` reports 0 errors for memcheck, racecheck, and initcheck.\n\n## Performance (RTX 3090, vs. 165 MCUPS scalar baseline)\n\n| grid | MCUPS | speedup |\n|---|---|---|\n| 64³ | 4,369 | 27× |\n| 128³ | 4,877 | 30× |\n| 256³ | 6,307 | 38× |\n| 384³ | 6,855 | 42× |\n| 512³ | 7,143 | **43×** |\n\nOne thing worth flagging: the kernel is FP64-throughput bound, not memory bound. At ~48 FP64 ops per cell update, 7.14 GCUPS is ~62% of the 3090's 556 GFLOP/s FP64 peak (higher in terms of actual instructions issued, since many contract to FMAs) — a GeForce part runs FP64 at 1/64 rate. On a datacenter GPU the same code would scale roughly with FP64 peak. I measured a variant that algebraically collapses the affine part of the chemical potential (`4.5*((c+1)e_AA + ...)` → a single FMA), worth another ~15–20%, but did not adopt it: it would forfeit the provable bit-exact equivalence above, which seemed the wrong trade for a benchmark port. Say the word if you'd prefer the extra speed."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":360,"cache_read_input_tokens":118581,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":360},"output_tokens":5,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"b40cf15e-2632-4174-af24-47ebc4cf64cb","uuid":"b7ee1860-1394-49f4-98d5-73f30885ac89","timestamp":"2026-09-02T05:03:50.626Z","request_id":"req_011Cee2ZpczcfWm93bjomFNw"}
